title: Recovery-Signer Crash Consistency

validation.scientific_correspondence: Every frozen P18-01..P18-16 test appeared explicitly as ok in the exact frozen-head job log; the same job concluded Ran 1090 tests and OK. Workflow success alone was not used as scientific proof.

supported_bounded_claims: On the tested same-host Ubuntu/Python/SQLite/OpenSSL prototype, parent-controlled external process termination at the frozen recovery-signer issuance boundaries did not manufacture permit authority.
Kills before durable issuance commit left no committed issuance authority after fresh reopen.
A kill after durable issuance commit but before response delivery preserved one issuance identity and retry returned the exact same permit/signature rather than minting duplicate authority.
A committed recovery identity remained non-rebindable across kill, restart and replay.
Minimum-side use-time validation required committed issuance evidence and the independent anti-rollback anchor, preventing pre-commit signed material from authorizing trusted-minimum mutation.
State drift after issuance was revalidated at minimum use time and stale authorization failed closed.
Concurrent retries after response loss converged on one exact permit/signature and one durable issuance identity.
Repeated signer restart preserved replay and rebinding memory.
A stale issuance-store snapshot could not silently resurrect a pre-issuance state against the independent anchor in the frozen vector.
After crash/replay recovery, clean next-step R2 to R3 authorization and minimum advancement remained live.
Models, reviewers, registry/root/minimum ordinary surfaces gained no signer, release, deploy or production authority from crash recovery.
explicit_nonclaims: OS-user, host-admin, kernel or hypervisor compromise resistance
security after joint compromise of signer key/store and independent anti-rollback anchor
atomicity between the issuance ledger commit and anti-rollback-anchor update under a kill precisely between those two durable writes
torn-write or crash consistency of the anti-rollback anchor itself
production, release, deploy or completion authority
retained_hygiene_debt: Pre-existing subprocess ResourceWarning messages from older Pilot 13/14 paths remain visible in the governed regression log and are not treated as Pilot 18 mechanism failures.
next_gap: The nearest unproven crash boundary is the two-store durability gap between issuance-ledger COMMIT and independent anti-rollback-anchor advancement, including kill/torn/stale/divergent anchor states and deterministic reconciliation.
